description: Indian FMCG / CPG sales terminology used by Cooper AI. Every question is checked against these terms (full forms, aliases and field slang) before it is interpreted. Basic formulas follow common Indian FMCG practice; where Pulse uses a specific formula, the metric_id links to the formula options in backend/app/catalog.py.

terms.definition: Sales billed by the company (or its C&F / super stockist) to distributors. Measured on invoices.
terms.basic_formula: Sum of net invoice value of non-cancelled invoices raised to distributors in the period

terms.definition: Sales billed by distributors to retailers / outlets.
terms.basic_formula: Sum of net invoice value of non-cancelled distributor-to-outlet invoices in the period

terms.definition: Sales from the retailer to the end consumer. Usually not captured in SFA data.
terms.basic_formula: Sum of retailer-to-consumer sales value (not available in Pulse for most companies)

terms.definition: Sales from a super stockist to a distributor. Pulse stores these together with primary sales.
terms.basic_formula: Sum of net invoice value from super stockist to distributors

terms.definition: Total value printed on invoices, including GST and other taxes, net of discounts.
terms.basic_formula: Sum of invoice total value (net value + taxes) for non-cancelled invoices

terms.definition: Value of orders booked by salesmen at outlets, before invoicing.
terms.basic_formula: Sum of net order value of non-cancelled orders booked in the period

terms.definition: Count of distinct orders booked at outlets.
terms.basic_formula: Count of distinct non-cancelled orders in the period

terms.definition: From the 1st of the current month up to today.
From the first day of the current (fiscal) quarter up to today.
From the first day of the company's financial year (usually 1 April in India) up to today.
Same date range as MTD, but in the previous month. Used for like-for-like comparison.
The same month one year earlier.
The last three months.
The last six months.
Change compared with the previous month.
terms.basic_formula: (This month - Last month) / Last month x 100

terms.definition: Change compared with the same period last year.
terms.basic_formula: (This year - Last year) / Last year x 100

terms.definition: Number of outlet visits (calls) made by field salesmen, productive or not.
terms.basic_formula: Count of distinct outlet visits (attendance records) in the period

terms.definition: Outlet visits that resulted in at least one order.
terms.basic_formula: Count of distinct visits marked productive (with an order) in the period

terms.definition: Visits planned for the day as per the beat / journey plan.
terms.basic_formula: Count of outlets scheduled on the day's beat plan

terms.full_form: Productive Call Percentage (Call Productivity / Strike Rate)
terms.definition: Share of visits that produced an order.
terms.basic_formula: PC / TC x 100

terms.definition: Number of distinct outlets visited at least once in the period.
terms.basic_formula: Count of distinct outlets visited

terms.definition: Number of distinct outlets that placed at least one order in the period.
terms.basic_formula: Count of distinct outlets with at least one productive order

terms.definition: Number of distinct outlets that received at least one invoice (bill) in the period. Also called ECO (Effective Coverage Outlets) in some companies.
terms.basic_formula: Count of distinct outlets with at least one non-cancelled invoice in the period

terms.definition: Billed outlets as a share of the outlets the team is supposed to serve.
terms.basic_formula: UBO / Assigned outlets x 100

terms.definition: Share of the outlets the team should cover that were actually visited.
terms.basic_formula: Visited outlets (UTC) / Assigned outlets on beat plan x 100

terms.definition: Share of the outlets the team should cover that actually ordered.
terms.basic_formula: Productive outlets (UPC) / Assigned outlets x 100

terms.definition: Share of the total outlet universe that stocks or bills the product.
terms.basic_formula: Outlets billed for the product / Total outlet universe x 100

terms.definition: Distribution weighted by outlet size (share of category sales made through outlets that stock the product).
terms.basic_formula: Category sales of outlets stocking the product / Total category sales x 100

terms.definition: Outlets that are live (not blocked) in the outlet master, or mapped to an active beat.
terms.basic_formula: Count of outlets not blocked in the outlet master

terms.definition: Outlets blocked or deactivated in the outlet master.
terms.basic_formula: Count of outlets marked blocked in the outlet master

terms.definition: Active outlets that have not been billed in a period, usually the last 3 months.
terms.basic_formula: Active outlets - Outlets billed in the last 3 months

terms.definition: Outlets added to the master during the period.
terms.basic_formula: Count of outlets created in the period

terms.definition: Average number of SKU lines ordered per productive call. Higher LPC means better range selling.
terms.basic_formula: Total order lines / Productive calls

terms.definition: Number of SKU lines in orders.
terms.basic_formula: Count of SKU lines across orders

terms.definition: Average value per invoice (or per order).
terms.basic_formula: Secondary sales value / Number of invoices

terms.definition: Average number of total calls made by each active salesman.
terms.basic_formula: TC / Number of salesmen who made calls

terms.definition: Time of day the salesman makes the first outlet call. Earlier usually means better market discipline.
terms.basic_formula: Average of each salesman's first call time per working day (company local time)

terms.definition: When the salesman starts the working day in the app.
Share of ordered quantity or value that was actually invoiced / delivered.
terms.basic_formula: Invoiced quantity / Ordered quantity x 100

terms.definition: A product is not available at the outlet or distributor.
How many days current stock will last at the current sales rate.
terms.basic_formula: Closing stock / Average daily sales

terms.definition: Document the distributor creates when stock from the company is received.
One specific sellable product variant (brand + size + pack).
Brand family such as Figaro or Bertolli. In Pulse this is the product division.
Group of SKUs such as Pure, Extra Virgin or Extra Light. In Pulse this is the product primary category.
SKUs every outlet of a type is expected to stock.
Products the company is pushing in the current period.
A newly launched product.
Highest price at which the product can be sold to consumers in India.
Price at which the distributor sells to the retailer.
Price at which the company sells to the distributor.
Price at which the company sells to the super stockist.
Discount or free goods offered to retailers or distributors to push sales.
Company's channel partner who buys from the company and sells to retailers in a territory.
Large stockist who supplies smaller distributors, usually in rural or far areas.
Company's warehouse agent who stores and dispatches stock to distributors.
A retail store that buys from the distributor.
Traditional independent stores (kiranas, chemists, paan shops) served via distributors.
Organised retail chains and supermarkets.
Bulk buyers who resell to smaller retailers.
A fixed set of outlets a salesman visits on a given day.
Fixed schedule of beats a salesman follows over a week or month.
Field salesman who visits outlets and books orders. DSR is paid by the distributor; ISR/TSI/SO are company roles.
Manages salesmen in an area / territory.
Manages ASMs across a region.
Manages RSMs across a zone (North, South, East, West).
Heads sales for the whole country.
A manager working in the market alongside the salesman.
A call made to an outlet that was not on the planned beat.
Top level of the sales geography, for example North, South, East, West.
Second level of the sales geography, below zone.
Area handled by one ASM / sales officer, below region.
One hundred thousand (1,00,000).
Ten million (1,00,00,000) = 100 lakh.
Shipping box that holds a fixed number of units of a SKU (the super unit in Pulse).
Single consumer packs.
